segments.heading: Overview
segments.text: Text effects are optional, shipped by and , not by . segments.text: Four-segment meter that visualizes password strength. Each segment has its own color, and a text label states the level in words.

segments.text: By default every segment keeps its own color, so a full bar shows red, orange, primary, and green. Add to paint all filled segments with the color of the current level instead.

segments.heading: Strength Colors
segments.text: The fill length and color follow the level, so the filled share of the bar tells the level at a glance: Fill Level Label Color Token ≤ 25% 1 Weak ≤ 50% 2 Fair ≤ 75% 3 Good ≤ 100% 4 Strong The bar has four segments, and each one has a fixed color token. A level fills that many segments from the start, so a full bar shows all four colors: Segment Color Token Default Light Default Dark Reached at 1 Red Light red Level 1 (Weak) 2 Orange/yellow Light yellow Level 2 (Fair) 3 Blue Light blue Level 3 (Good) 4 Green Light green Level 4 (Strong) Unfilled Light gray Dark gray Empty track Level 0 fills no segment. With , all filled segments use the color of the current level instead (red at level 1, orange at level 2, blue at level 3, green at level 4).

segments.text: Level 0 (Empty): No password entered Label: "Enter a password" or similar Bar: No segment filled (subtle track only) Level 1 (Weak): Very short passwords (< 6 characters) Only lowercase or only numbers Common words, sequential characters Label: "Weak" or "Too weak" Bar: 1 segment (red) Level 2 (Fair): Short passwords (6-8 characters) Two character types (lowercase + numbers) Some complexity but lacking Label: "Fair" or "Could be stronger" Bar: 2 segments (red, orange) Level 3 (Good): Medium length (8-12 characters) Three character types (lowercase + uppercase + numbers) Good complexity Label: "Good" or "Strong enough" Bar: 3 segments (red, orange, primary) Level 4 (Strong): Long passwords (12+ characters) All character types (lowercase + uppercase + numbers + symbols) High entropy, not in breach lists Label: "Strong" or "Excellent" Bar: 4 segments (red, orange, primary, green)

segments.heading: Rules and Pitfalls
segments.text: 1. Always give items a base span Inside a 12-column grid, items without any class occupy 1 column (1/12 width). Start every item with (or whichever span you want at the smallest size): 2. Containers narrower than 320px have no rule The smallest breakpoint is at 320px. Below that, items fall back to span 1. This only matters for extremely narrow containers. If needed, set on items. 3. Don't mix with responsive classes (base span classes) are re-declared inside the container block, after / rules. At 768px+, they override and jump back to full width: If you must use , also set an class so it wins. 4. Container can't size itself from content removes the grid's intrinsic width. In a shrink-to-fit parent (flex row, flex column with ), the grid collapses to a sliver (~176px with default gap). Give it explicit width: 5. Only spans 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 There are no responsive classes for 5, 7, 9, 10, or 11. 6. Use , not plain Span classes assume 12 equal tracks. Plain uses auto-fit tracks, so would mean "six auto-fit tracks" instead of 6/12. 7. Gap from Override per grid with . Without it, the gap follows the token (12px, 16px or 24px depending on the viewport).

segments.heading: Foundation
segments.text: CSS reset and base element styling for bare HTML elements.

segments.heading: Overview
segments.text: EN-CSS provides a minimal, modern foundation that normalizes browser defaults while preserving semantic HTML behavior. The foundation consists of two layers: Reset ( ) - Removes browser inconsistencies (box-sizing, margin, form inheritance) Base ( ) - Styles bare HTML elements with typography, spacing, and colors Philosophy: Start with sensible defaults for semantic HTML, then enhance with utility classes and components as needed.

segments.heading: Reset

segments.heading: Accessibility Features
segments.text: Reduced motion support: Automatically respects user's motion preferences: Focus visibility: All interactive elements get focus rings by default (in ):

segments.heading: Why This Reset?
segments.text: What we DON'T reset: Font sizes (let headings be semantic) Line heights (preserve readability) Display values (keep semantic meaning) Colors (theme-dependent, handled in base) What we DO reset: Box-sizing (consistent sizing model) Margins (prevent collapse issues) Form inheritance (consistent cross-browser) Media sizing (responsive by default)

segments.heading: Maximize a Panel
segments.text: The button toggles the class, updates , locks page scroll and moves focus into the panel. Pressing Escape inside the panel closes it. All behavior is inline in the markup; there is no script block. The border and radius classes are removed while the panel is maximized, because the utility does not reset them.

segments.heading: Native Fullscreen API

The class supplies the background (and ), so the element is not black or transparent.

segments.heading: Bleed
segments.text: Utilities that make a block element sit flush against the edges of its parent, or of the screen. They remove the left and right border, the corner radius, and the shadow. The top and bottom borders stay as separators. Bleed utilities are part of the extended utilities ( , or ).

segments.heading: Always Bleed
segments.text: applies at every screen size. The dashed frame stands in for the parent.

segments.heading: Only on Small Screens
segments.text: , , and apply only below the breakpoint. Use them to save horizontal space on mobile while keeping the normal look on larger screens.

segments.heading: Breakpoints
segments.text: Class Applies when the viewport is any width narrower than 480px narrower than 768px narrower than 1024px narrower than 1280px The suffix means "below this breakpoint", the same as , and . It is the opposite of and the other display utilities, where the suffix means "from this breakpoint up". Each range is the exact complement of the matching rule, so no viewport width falls in a gap.

segments.heading: Other Components

segments.text: All rules live in the last cascade layer ( ), so they win over the border, radius and shadow of any component without . Hover and other state shadows set by a component are removed as well, for the same reason. Effects ( ) load after these utilities. If you combine with a shadow effect class, the effect wins. segments.heading: Extended Utilities
segments.text: Optional utilities on top of the Core Utilities: larger type and spacing steps, breakpoint and fluid spacing, negative margins, spacing between children, responsive display, extra animations and touch targets.

segments.heading: Overview
segments.text: Extended utilities cover needs that are less common than the core set, so they are not part of . They use the same tokens, the same prefix and the same cascade layer ( ) as the core utilities, and they load after them. On one element, an extended class usually wins over a core class that sets the same property, because it loads later. What's included: Text extras (2xl-6xl sizes, tracking, leading, line clamp) Large spacing (6, 8, 10 for padding, margin and gap) Borders per side, shadows, focus ring, opacity and backdrop blur Viewport sizing, hidden scrollbars and corner positions Responsive display ( , , , per breakpoint), range visibility and print Breakpoint ( , , ) and fluid spacing Negative margins, with gutter and inset bleed margins Space between children ( , ) Extra animations (directional slide, bounce, zoom) Touch targets Edge-to-edge blocks ( ) are part of the Core Utilities, not of this set.

segments.heading: Browser support
segments.text: The support floor is Baseline 2025 (features that are Baseline "newly available" by the end of 2025, i.e. early 2026). It is defined in one place, : The minimum browser versions are derived from (not written by hand) and shared by , and . The versions used for the last build are stored in → . To move the floor, change and rebuild. Because the floor is modern, LightningCSS no longer adds transpilation fallbacks for features such as , nesting or , which keeps the output smaller. Before using a new CSS feature in source, check its Baseline status on MDN or web.dev. Features that are not Baseline yet must be wrapped in .

Buttons, badges, and alerts automatically use correct foreground colors ( , etc.) for accessibility. Form control borders: Inputs, selects, and interactive controls use (≥3:1 contrast per WCAG 1.4.11) instead of . This ensures all form elements meet accessibility standards. Scale system: Three independent axes control sizing: (global, backwards compatible) (typography only) (spacing and control heights) Components never read the scale axes directly—they use derived tokens like and .

segments.heading: Best practices
segments.text: One bundle per project. Every bundle includes the foundation, so importing two bundles duplicates code (the exception is , which is meant to be added on top). Framework first, your styles last. Your own CSS written without automatically wins over all EN-CSS layers. Add components incrementally. Start from a small bundle and import single extended files as you need them.

segments.text: Can I import both and ? No. Each includes the foundation. Pick one, then add single components. What is in each bundle? See PRESETS.md.
